rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 5 (657.5, best) used 12 mm sensors at x = ±0.02 m, y = 0.05 m, mass 0.4 kg, base_speed 1.1, kp 6, kd 0.8, ki 0.02. Oval 18/20, s-bend 20/20, slalom 0/20 (progress 0.35, 1.8 line-loss events, max_error at the 0.06 m limit). Iteration 7 widened the span to ±0.025 m: oval improved to 20/20 with 0.15 line losses, slalom line losses fell from 1.8 to 1.05, but s-bend dropped to 15/20 and slalom progress fell to 0.28. Iteration 6 showed that lowering base_speed does not help the slalom. The slalom is the only track that never finishes, and it fails through excursions at sharp direction changes. Sensor lead is the lever I have not tested alone. Iteration 2 moved y to 0.06 together with other changes, so its effect is unknown.

Change: keep the iteration 7 geometry (span ±0.025 m, 12 mm sensors) and move the sensors forward from y = 0.05 to y = 0.06 m. Controller, mass, speed and line-loss handling are unchanged, so this is a single-variable test against iteration 7. The forward sensors see the line about 10 mm earlier, which gives the controller more time to steer before a sharp bend.

Expected result: slalom progress above 0.35 with line losses at or below 1.0, oval completion at or above 0.9, and s-bend completion recovering toward 0.9 or better. Hypotheses: (a) forward lead reduces slalom off-track events; (b) if s-bend falls further, the wider span is the cause and the span should return to ±0.02 m while keeping y = 0.06; (c) if slalom line losses stay near 1.0 with no progress gain, the limit is steering gain or kd, and the next test should change kd (to about 1.0) alone.

Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation on each track, plus control_effort to check steering load.
